title: Joystick Control
description: Learn to map analog data from a joystick to control the speed and direction of DC motors using PWM and H-bridge.
objectives: Understand how an analog joystick works
Map analog values (0-1023) to motor speed
Implement direction control using L298N H-bridge
Create an intuitive control system for mobile robot

wiring.description: Connection diagram between Pico W, joystick and H-bridge
warnings: ⚠️ NEVER connect 12V directly to Pico! Pico uses 3.3V logic.
⚠️ Always connect common GND between Pico, H-bridge and battery.
⚠️ Check all connections before turning on power.
⚠️ Use a separate battery for motors, not USB power.

theory.joystick: An analog joystick has two potentiometers (X and Y axes) that vary from 0 to 3.3V. The Pico W reads these values through ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter) which transforms voltage into digital values from 0 to 65535.
theory.pwm: PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) controls motor speed by varying the width of electrical pulses. A 50% duty cycle means the motor receives power 50% of the time, resulting in half maximum speed.
theory.hbridge: The H-bridge allows controlling motor direction by reversing polarity. With IN1=HIGH and IN2=LOW the motor spins one way; inverting, it spins the opposite way. ENA controls speed via PWM.

steps.title: Circuit Assembly
steps.description: Build the circuit following the connection diagram
details: Connect joystick to Pico ADC pins (GP26 and GP27)
Connect H-bridge to Pico digital pins
Connect DC motors to H-bridge OUT terminals
Connect 12V battery to H-bridge (VCC and GND)
Make sure all GNDs are connected (common ground)

steps.title: BIPES Configuration
steps.description: Open project in BIPES and configure blocks
details: Access BIPES project link (see below)
Locate pin configuration blocks
Configure GP26 and GP27 as ADC inputs
Configure GP0-GP5 as digital/PWM outputs
Observe mapping logic in main block

steps.title: Upload and Test
details: Connect Pico W to computer via USB
In BIPES, click 'Run' to upload
Wait for code transfer
Move joystick and observe motor movement
Joystick forward = robot moves forward
Joystick backward = robot moves backward
Joystick left/right = turns

steps.title: Adjustments and Calibration
details: If motors are inverted, swap IN1 with IN2
Adjust maximum duty cycle if motors are too fast
Add deadzone in joystick center
Test different response curves (linear, exponential)

code.pseudocode:
# Read joystick values
value_x = read_adc(GP26)  # 0-65535
value_y = read_adc(GP27)  # 0-65535

# Map to -100 to +100
speed = map(value_y, 0, 65535, -100, 100)
direction = map(value_x, 0, 65535, -100, 100)

# Calculate individual motor speeds
left_motor = speed + direction
right_motor = speed - direction

# Limit values
left_motor = constrain(left_motor, -100, 100)
right_motor = constrain(right_motor, -100, 100)

# Control motors
control_motor_a(left_motor)
control_motor_b(right_motor)
code.notes: In BIPES, this logic is implemented visually using mapping and PWM control blocks.

solutions: Check if battery is connected and charged
Confirm ENA and ENB jumpers are enabled on H-bridge
Test PWM pin output with an LED

troubleshooting.problem: Motor spins in only one direction
solutions: Check IN1 and IN2 (or IN3 and IN4) connections
Confirm digital pins are configured correctly
Try swapping motor connections on H-bridge
Check if GP26 and GP27 are configured as ADC
Add small delay between ADC readings

troubleshooting.problem: Motors shake or make strange noise
solutions: Check if power supply provides enough current (min. 1A)
Reduce PWM frequency if too high
Make sure motors aren't mechanically blocked

challenges.title: Challenge 1: Deadzone
challenges.description: Implement a ±10% deadzone in joystick center to avoid unwanted movements when joystick is at rest.

challenges.title: Challenge 2: Smooth Control
challenges.description: Add gradual acceleration instead of abrupt speed changes. Use a moving average filter on read values.

challenges.title: Challenge 3: Turbo Mode
challenges.description: Implement a joystick button that activates 'turbo mode' doubling maximum motor speed.
